subject: MAP: NovaMed POC access & acceptance - proposed timeline
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
To: Sophie Yang <sophie.yang@novamed.com>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>, Aditya Rao <aditya_rao@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 30 Aug 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: MAP: NovaMed POC access & acceptance - proposed timeline

Hi Sophie —

Thanks again for taking the call last week. Per our MAP conversation, attached is a draft mutual action plan (MAP_v0.3.xlsx) that lays out the technical prerequisites we need to get your evaluation environment running and an acceptance checklist for the POC. High-level items included:

- API key provisioning and role permissions (we create an evaluation API key scoped to your org)
- Org setup: invite users + service account for CI/CD testing
- IP allowlist entries for our ingress endpoints and the POC runner
- VPC peering configuration and maintenance window
- Acceptance criteria for performance & functional validation (latency targets, sample prompt tests)

Proposed timeline (subject to your procurement window):
- T+1: API key + org invite issued by our SRE (you provide user emails)
- T+2: IP allowlist entries confirmed by your network team
- T+3: VPC peering initiation (handshake)
- T+5: End-to-end smoke tests by NovaMed + Redwood (acceptance gating)

We included a simple network_diagram.png to show the recommended peering/subnet rules. Can you confirm two things: (1) who on your side owns network/VPC peering so we can loop them in, and (2) whether the proposed acceptance window of 5 business days after peering fits your schedule?

Next steps from our side once you confirm: we will create the eval org, generate scoped API keys, and schedule a 1-hour handoff meeting for the peering runbook.

Thanks — looking forward to getting this moving.

Best,
Marissa Cole
Senior Sales Engineer | Redwood Inference
marissa.cole@redwood.ai
+1 (415) 555-0192

Marissa —

Thanks for the clear plan and the files. High level looks good. A couple of quick clarifications before I loop in our network and procurement teams: 

1) VPC peering: we need to understand the expected maintenance window and whether cross-account IAM roles are required for the handshake.
2) IP allowlist: can you provide the ASN and the CIDR ranges you will use for the POC runner?

Procurement is on copy — procurement will need the MAP spreadsheet and the proposed billing terms before we can sign off. Alex (cc) will own the network side; Alex, can you confirm who should be the technical contact for peering?

Thanks Sophie — good questions. Quick answers below and plan for next actions.

1) Maintenance window: we recommend a 2-hour window for the peering handshake and initial route propagation; this is non-disruptive if scheduled off-peak. We do not require cross-account IAM for the basic peering; it is a standard peering connection with route exchange. If you prefer a cross-account role for automation, we can support that as an add-on.

2) CIDRs/ASN: attached network_diagram.png shows the public egress CIDRs we will use for the POC runner (10.142.0.0/16 for the sandbox NAT, and the public egress ranges listed on tab ‘NetworkRanges’ in MAP_v0.3.xlsx). Our ASN for peering is 64512.

Action items:
- Karthik will schedule a 30-minute network sync with Alex and your network lead to do the peering handshake (I’ve asked Karthik to propose times).
- We’ll provision the evaluation org and generate an API key scoped to the MAP test set once procurement provides the PO or signs the MAP.
- Once peering is confirmed, we will run the smoke tests within 48 hours.

I’ve attached the same files for convenience. Karthik — can you take point on the network sync and loop Aditya for billing/usage estimates?

Hi all —

I'll take the network sync. Proposed windows (PST):
- Wed Sep 1: 10:00–10:30 
- Wed Sep 1: 15:00–15:30 
- Thu Sep 2: 09:00–09:30

Please confirm which works for Alex / NovaMed network lead. I’ll circulate a short runbook for the peering handshake (steps, expected route propagation times, and rollback instructions). Key timeline once we have a confirmed slot:

1) T+0: Runbook review and peering handshake (30 mins)
2) T+0+2h: route propagation check and IP allowlist verification
3) T+1: Redwood provisions eval org and issues scoped API key to NovaMed service account
4) T+2: Combined smoke tests executed by NovaMed with Redwood on the call (acceptance targets documented in MAP_v0.3.xlsx tab 'Acceptance')

Procurement: we have a MAP spreadsheet attached — can you confirm whether a signed MAP or a PO will be the preferred path for your contracting? We can provide a short acceptance amendment via DocuSign to avoid a long SOW for this eval. Link to the signable MAP: https://app.hubspot.com/deals/34921
